significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish the form-(iii) ordering that, after holding billing co-occurrence constant, “mechanistically linked diseases are closer than diseases that merely co-occur due to demographics or coding artifacts,” together with a form-(ii) causal coupling whereby a “disease-mechanism direction” selectively shifts risks for downstream conditions. This establishes a mechanism-aligned representational phenomenon and a bounded model-internal causal role—not the biological mechanisms themselves—and would constrain expected embedding neighborhoods and risk-response patterns in prediction-oriented systems such as Med-BERT (Rasmy et al., 2021). Verified false, it would favor coding/co-occurrence explanations over pathophysiological interpretations of this geometry, although it would not rule out mechanism information elsewhere in the models; the two branches are therefore distinguishable and informative. In the topic-substitution check, the generic question of whether scientific representations match established mechanisms would merit only the topic median, while the co-occurrence-controlled ordering and downstream selective coupling are claim-specific reasons for scoring above it.

reach.justification: The named handles are the “mechanism-alignment score” as an auditing diagnostic and the “disease-mechanism direction” as an intervention, but neither is presented as a validated predictor of clinical failure, so their lead time is principally post-hoc model analysis rather than an operational ex-ante warning. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive prediction survives as a relation—mechanism-linked pairs should remain closer than co-occurrence-only pairs and steering should preferentially affect “mechanistically downstream conditions”—rather than merely supplying an open-ended search procedure. The hypothesis speaks broadly of “clinical foundation models,” and its likely users include interpretability researchers and teams auditing clinical risk models, though it does not yet hand clinicians a deployment threshold or patient-level decision rule. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: the topic alone supplies no reusable metric or intervention, whereas these two quoted handles and the transferable conditional ordering do.
